lines.en: I hesitantly tap on Tsubasa’s name in my phone...knowing that, if she answers, I’ll have a hard time coming out of the conversation unscathed.
Because she’s talked to me before about what’s typically done with girls in rich families — how they’re traded like cattle.
I’ve just never expected it would happen to the ones that I know. Let alone the ones she’s raised.
And as always, I just can’t understand why she’d do this.
: Hello? Akira?
If she even is doing it at all and Chinami wasn’t just...dramatically misunderstanding something.
: Hey, Tsubasa...By any chance, are you free right now?

: Hmm...That’s a difficult question to answer as the freedom I typically have is almost always inhibited by the constant possibility that I may need to stop what I’m doing to address some sort of conflict or trade.
: But I suppose I can find the time to fit you in should you need something from me. And I assume that you do as you wouldn’t call otherwise.
: So I can’t call you just to hang out?
: Of course you can. I’d just likely refuse since your time is better spent with my daughters instead of me.
: Yeah, so that’s kind of why I want to talk to you. It’s about them.
: Oh my. Touka isn’t pregnant, is she? Because I simply just don’t have the time to deal with that right now.
: If she is, it’s a miracle as I’ve yet to even lay a finger on her.
: I’m both delighted and offended at the same time. How odd.
: Tsubasa, it’s your other daughter I want to talk to you about.
: Oh dear. You got that one pregnant instead? That sounds quite painful for both of you, but welcome to the family regardless.
: Again, haven’t laid a finger on her. I just...heard something recently that-
: Let me guess — Tsukasa mentioned something about an arranged marriage to Chinami, who subsequently relayed the message to you out of fear for her friend’s well-being.
: And now you’re upset because it means someone else is going to get to her before you do. Is that correct?
: No. That’s not correct. I’m just worried about how Tsukasa feels in regard to this.
: With all due respect, Akira — Tsukasa is not your daughter to worry about. Perhaps that energy would be best spent on Ami instead?
: Ami...hasn’t come home in a while.
: Ahh, then I take it this is parenting withdrawal? Tsukasa’s home now if you would like to come over and pamper her. I’m sure she’d be delighted.
: Can I just come talk to you instead? This is difficult over the phone since I can’t fall back on how much bigger I am than you when you make me feel weak and powerless.
: Is this flirting again? What should I say back?
: Just tell me I can come over.
: You can come wherever you like, Akira. It makes no difference to me.
: Uhh...cool. Then I guess I’m-
: Master Arakawa — right this way, please.
: Oh, excellent! That was even quicker than normal. Do tell Daigo I said hello.
: You sent a-
: See you soon, Akira. Oh — and I have a surprise waiting. Ciao!
: Tsuba-
: Master Arakawa-
: Tsubasa says hello.
I hop in the back of the limo and prepare myself for what is already shaping up to be another eventful talk with Tsubasa. And one that comes with a “surprise” at that.
I just hope that whatever this surprise is doesn’t end up with me chained to a wall or forced into indentured servitude.
But I...suddenly realize that isn’t what she was referring to at all.
: So quick again! Daigo’s rapidly becoming my favorite driver out of all of them. I might have to give him a raise at this rate.
: Anyway — you already know Yuki, yes? What do you think of her hair? Isn’t this much better than that ugly, faded blonde?
: Her hair is the last thing I’m concerned about. I haven’t seen her since-
: Since I nearly fuckin’ died in front of you, yeah. What the hell is he doing here? You didn’t tell me he was coming.
: It was a surprise for both of you! Now, you no longer have to mope around all upset that you haven’t seen him in so long.
: What?! I never-
: She simply won’t stop talking about you. It’s actually made me quite jealous!
: That’s a lie! I haven’t-
: Wha-?! Dude! The fuck are you doing?!
: Just let it happen. I’m glad to see you’re okay.
: Even after I...was a huge fuckin’ asshole to you? And tried to take your money and shit? Why? Thought that bridge was as good as torched.
: You also asked me to come over and fuck you, so it’s not like it was all evil.
: I...don’t remember doin’ that. But yeah, still alive. Just...here now.
: And it’s all thanks to Nee-sama that I-
: N...Nee-sama?
: Hmph! You’ve never hugged me like that...
: I ain’t even doin’ all the huggin’! He just grabbed me outta nowhere!
: Nee-sama? Wait, you two aren’t-
: We ain’t actually related, no. I’ve just always called her that.
: So are you, like...her bodyguard now? Or...
: I think I’m more like a pet than anything at this point.
: Bad dog! Heel!
: See what I mean?
: Yeah, but...I can ask more about that later. Are you doing okay? How long do you-
: Yuki’s health is no immediate concern and the Tsukioka Foundation is fully covering any and all treatment she may need. It’s the least I can do.
: Callin’ it the “least” you can do when you’re savin’ my life is the fuckin’ understatement of the century. I’d be dying without you, Nee-sama.
: In that case! May I be hugged next?
: Sure. Go get her, Akira.
: Tch! Why is it that I can have everything in life besides the one thing I want?
: This is...an interesting side of you, Tsubasa.
: Is it? How so?
: You just seem more...relaxed, I guess? There’s no guard up when you talk to Yuki like there is when you talk to me.
: Nonsense. Why on earth would I have my guard up around you, Akira? You’re among the least intimidating men I’ve ever encountered.
: She just likes fuckin’ with me. Kinda like a big sister pickin’ on the little sister sorta thing.
: So Tsubasa’s the older sister in this relationship?
: Well, yeah. She’s older than me.
: Wait, so how old is-
: Yuki — didn’t you have some matters to attend to tonight? I practically had to beg just to have you wait around for the surprise.
: Oh, shit! You’re right. I totally forgot.
: I’m goin’ back to the bar to talk to Sara and shit. Ain’t sure if she’ll give me my job back, but I at least want to apologize for bein’ an asshole to her after she went out of her way for me.
: Plus, she doesn’t even know about the cancer thing yet and...yeah.
: But anyway — I’m gonna be here for a little while. And...I’m sorry to you too. I’m just...you know...kind of a terrible person. So shit like that might happen sometimes.
: As an equally terrible person, I understand.
: It was nice seeing you, Yuki. I’m glad you’re okay.
: Yeah! Uhh...
: Bye.
Yuki leaves the room and...wait, why am I here again?
: So —you wanted to talk to me about Tsukasa?
: Oh, right. You’re not, like...actually considering marrying her off to some random guy, are you?
: He’d be no random guy, Akira. None of her potential suitors fit that pairing of words. They’re valuable assets from upstanding families who, more than likely, would treat her well.
: She’s a kid...
: Which is probably one more reason why she has so many suitors. Men in power really seem to jump at that sort of thing, don’t they?
: And you’re just going to endorse it? You don’t care at all about what this would mean for her as a person?
: What would it mean for her as a person, Akira? Because, from what I understand, you haven’t talked to Tsukasa about this at all. Just one of her friends.
: But that friend knows her well and can tell that she’s scared.
: You’re scared right now and no harm has befallen you yet. Who’s to say the same won’t happen to Tsukasa as well?
: You want this then? To just...offload her on someone else?
: Not at all. As I said — there are valuable assets all over this city willing to merge into the Tsukioka Foundation for the right price. And there will always be things money can’t buy.
: So you intend to just buy them with your daughter’s hand in marriage?
: I don’t. My husband does. And this company is even more his child than the girls are. I imagine Touka would be in the same boat if she were not the heir apparent.
: What I’m doing is mediating the facilitation of his desires as that is my role in both the company and this family.
: But isn’t it your role as a mother to make sure your children are happy and safe?
: Indeed it is. Which is why I’d not hesitate to call this off should Tsukasa verbalize her hesitancy. Even mere unease would do the trick.
: It’s...that simple? Really? You don’t have anything else up your sleeve?
: I always have something up my sleeve, Akira. You have to in this line of work.
: Tomonori may be the family head, but do you really think I’m the type to gleefully allow someone else to pull my strings?
: When you say shit about “facilitating his desires” then yeah, I’m sort of forced to think that.
: I say what I need to say to protect the things I love. But sometimes, it’s the opposite.
: Sometimes, the things I don’t say are the ones that ring the loudest...or make the biggest differences. Which is why I’m sure you’ll understand what I’m doing in time.
: But for now — I imagine I must look pretty evil, don’t I?
: You’d look a lot worse if I didn’t find out five minutes ago that you saved my friend’s life.
: I’ve done no such thing. It takes far more than just money to defeat cancer.
: I’m just giving Yuki the tools she needs to fight the battle. But she’s the one who will ultimately need to save her own life.
: You’re helping her either way.
: As I’ve said — I protect the things I love. So why do you imagine that what I’m doing with Tsukasa is any different?
: It’s just...a confusing situation for me to hear from one of Tsukasa’s friends that she’s so scared of such a mature thing at her age.
: Confusing because you feel bad for her? Or because you’re attracted to her?
: I’m not-
: I saw what you did in her room, Akira.
: And almost right after I told you to never cum for anyone other than a Tsukioka in my house again.
: It’s like you disobeyed me on purpose. The audacity.
: Though, I suppose you may have found a loophole. And I suppose that you may have been cumming for Tsukasa despite being so...deep inside of your subordinate.
: You’ve been a very, very bad boy.
: That was...not a good night for me.
: Oh, I’m not looking for an excuse. You’re not in any trouble.
: As far as I’m concerned, what you did in there was no different from a live demonstration of the same brand of sexual intercourse she’d see if she looked it up online.
: Which she’s been doing quite frequently as of late. The poor girl doesn’t realize I can see her browsing history right from my telephone. Isn’t technology so fascinating now?
: I’m not...attracted to her, though. That was just a mistake I made in the heat of the moment.
: Bullshit. You know I have eyes everywhere and you knew you’d be caught. You dragged that woman to Tsukasa’s room for one reason and one reason only. You wanted to plant a seed.
: And no — I’m not talking about the type you planted in her. I’m talking about the type that wakes a curious little girl up.
: And in that regard — bravo, Akira. You’ve done it. But what will you do next? What’s the next phase of your plan? Because you need to hurry now, don’t you? The clock is ticking.
: If you don’t act quickly, you might never get another chance to fuck some woman in front of my youngest daughter. And that’s far more boring for me too, so I’m rooting for you.
: You’re...rooting for me.
: I kind of have to. I don’t have much of a choice when all is said and done.
: I wouldn’t be too worried if I were you, though. Even if the video does get out, the audio is barely audible and the footage is rather grainy.
: You...have it on video?
: Either that or I’m lying. Which one is it, do you think?
: Tsubasa...what do you want from me? Just tell me instead of trying to blackmail me all the time.
: Well, where’s the fun in that?
: There isn’t any. There doesn’t have to be. Because this might be fun for you, but it’s terrible for me. And the fact that I’m being constantly pushed into making the worst possible decisions is-
: Blah, blah, blah. Sometimes you have to force someone to do certain things or blah, blah, blah. I can’t remember how it goes.
: Can’t...remember how what goes?
: The thing. I’m sure you’ve heard it before, no?
: I...don’t really know. But either way, I can’t just...do that to Tsukasa if that’s what you’re trying to push me to do.
: Because I’m sure it sounds weird, but...I kind of care about her. And I don’t want to hurt her like that because I’ve seen what it turns other girls into.
: Do what? I’m oblivious and stupid. I don’t know what you’re alluding to.
: You know exactly what I’m alluding to. And if you somehow honestly don’t, all you need to do is look up Tsukasa’s search history again for a reminder.
: Hah! Now, now, Akira — we need to give her some privacy, don’t we?
: But we also need to make sure she’s not too ill-prepared for her pending and potentially very scary future...assuming nothing gets in the way of that.
: So I’m proposing that you add a new subject to whatever sort of...curriculum you’re using for her tutoring.
: And I’m sure you know what that subject is as it won’t be the first time you’ve tutored a girl her age in it. Do you understand what I mean?
: I...know what you mean. I just don’t know how you know.
: You don’t need to. Just play your part and I’ll play mine.
: One thing to note, though — us Tsukiokas are “hands-on” learners. Do with that information what you will.
: What are you reaching for-
: Tsukasa? Can you come to my office for a moment, dear?
: Tsubasa...what are you-
: You don’t have any plans tonight, do you? I figure I should be here for at least the first session if Tsukasa is going to learn sexual education from a man as unpredictable as you.
: Now? Seriously? I haven’t even agreed yet. This isn’t-
: Oh, Akira. You don’t have a choice! And neither do I — so let’s just make the most of this, shall we?
